# .gui (dotgui)

> .gui is an open, text-based file format for user interfaces  what .svg is to
> graphics, .gui is to UI. A .gui file is a zip package: design.guix (plain XML
> markup carrying frames, stacks, text, images, shapes, design tokens, fonts,
> and effects), an assets/ folder, and a preview.webp thumbnail. AI agents can
> read and write it directly; a deterministic, zero-AI toolchain validates,
> lints, scores, and renders it; any browser or design tool can display it.

Key facts:
- Only validation is required to produce a file; render and score are optional.
- A closed 53-role vocabulary (role="button", role="nav-bar", …) makes files self-describing.
- Quality is scored on CCAC (Clean, Consistent, Accessible, Comprehensible)  local, offline, zero-AI.
- The format, engine, CLI, and embed library are open source and free.

## Documentation

- [Full spec and toolchain docs](https://dotgui.org/llms-full.txt): everything below concatenated as one markdown file
- [Spec Reference](https://dotgui.org/spec/): every element, attribute, and token type
- [Role vocabulary](https://dotgui.org/spec/roles/): the 53 recognized UI roles
- [Quality model](https://dotgui.org/spec/quality/): the CCAC scoring spec

## Toolchain

- [gui CLI](https://dotgui.org/cli/): read, write, lint, render, and package .gui files; `gui setup` installs the dotgui skill into AI agents
- [@dotgui/kit](https://dotgui.org/kit/): the reference engine  parser, validator, renderer, scorer in one deterministic package
- [@dotgui/embed](https://dotgui.org/embed/): render .gui files on any website with one CDN script
- [Figma plugin](https://dotgui.org/figma/): export any Figma layer as a .gui file

## Guides

- [.gui vs CSS: a file format vs a styling language](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-css/): CSS styles a document that already exists somewhere else. .gui is the document: structure, layout, and appearance in one file, with no cascade to fight.
- [.gui vs HTML: a closed vocabulary vs an open runtime](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-html/): HTML is a programming surface that happens to describe UI. .gui is a static, closed vocabulary that always terminates in the same picture, everywhere.
- [.gui vs Figma files: portable text vs a vendor’s app](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-figma/): A Figma file only exists inside Figma. A .gui file is plain text in a zip: readable, diffable, and versionable without opening any design tool.
- [.gui vs a screenshot or PNG mockup](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-screenshots/): A picture is a dead end: an agent has to guess spacing, hierarchy, and color from pixels. A .gui file hands those values over directly, already structured.
- [.gui vs SVG: graphics format vs interface format](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-svg/): SVG made graphics text. .gui borrows that idea but is purpose-built for interface layout and semantics: things SVG was never designed to express.
- [Prompting your AI agent to build a .gui file](https://dotgui.org/guides/prompting-your-agent/): gui setup teaches your own agent the format. Here’s the mental model and what to actually say.
- [Common mistakes AI agents make in .gui files](https://dotgui.org/guides/common-agent-mistakes/): An agent that hasn’t been taught the format brings habits over from HTML and CSS that don’t belong in .gui. Here are the five that show up most.
- [Spacing in .gui: use gap, not an empty row](https://dotgui.org/guides/spacing-and-gaps/): The single most common habit agents bring over from HTML/CSS: and the one-attribute fix.
- [How to get a good CCAC score](https://dotgui.org/guides/ccac-score/): The four levels explained on /spec/quality, turned into concrete things to actually go fix.
- [Structuring a screen: row vs col vs grid](https://dotgui.org/guides/layout-row-col-grid/): Three layout elements cover almost every screen. Here’s how to pick between them without guessing.
- [Making AI-generated UI not look generic](https://dotgui.org/guides/avoiding-generic-ui/): The tells of an unedited AI-generated screen, and the structural (not aesthetic) fixes .gui makes available.
- [.gui is not a runtime: it’s a file you open and see](https://dotgui.org/guides/not-a-runtime/): The most common misread is that .gui is another framework you have to set up and run. It isn’t. Like an image, a .gui file stands on its own: you open it and see the interface, with no runtime required.
- [What problem does .gui actually solve?](https://dotgui.org/guides/what-problem/): The honest version: .gui isn’t trying to replace HTML, CSS, or your design tool. It adds one missing thing: a portable, throwaway design layer for the AI era.
- [Does .gui store layout intent or fixed pixels?](https://dotgui.org/guides/intent-vs-geometry/): The question that decides whether a UI format is worth having: does it record where things landed, or the rules that put them there? .gui stores intent, which is also its hardest spec problem.
- [Versioning, interactivity, and the conformance corpus](https://dotgui.org/guides/roadmap/): Where the format is (v0.2), where it’s going (v1.0 visual completeness, v2.0 motion), and the honest answer to "the ecosystem is the existential question."
- [.gui vs XAML, QML, and GTK .ui: interchange, not a runtime](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-xaml/): The most common reaction to .gui is "isn’t this just XAML?" It has the same markup shape and a different job: those are UI languages bound to a runtime; .gui is a portable target that can emit them.
- [.gui vs React and Vue: a file format, not a UI framework](https://dotgui.org/guides/vs-react-vue/): A question that comes up fast: "why is the dotgui site built in Vue, not .gui?" Because .gui isn’t a framework you deploy; it’s the design the framework gets built from. Here’s the distinction.
- [Handoff, pixel-perfection, and your component library](https://dotgui.org/guides/handoff-and-fidelity/): The fair developer objection: "a designer sends me a .gui, AI interprets it, it won’t be pixel-perfect, and it won’t map to our internal components." True, and not what .gui is claiming to do.

## Examples

Real .gui files to read and learn from. Each page renders the file live and
shows its full source; the raw design.guix links below return the plain-text
.gui markup directly — no download or unzip needed.

- [Skeuomorphic Album](https://dotgui.org/examples/skeuomorphic-album/) — mobile; A skeuomorphic mobile album screen with a warm cream paper background and deep groove-black accents, styling track listings like the label of a spinning vinyl record. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/skeuomorphic-album/raw)
- [Bloom — Product Page](https://dotgui.org/examples/bloom-pdp/) — mobile; A Material You product detail page for a plant shop, built on a soft off-white canvas with a deep forest-green primary and lime containers for a fresh, botanical feel. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/bloom-pdp/raw)
- [Flight Results — Dark](https://dotgui.org/examples/flight-results-mobile/) — mobile; A dark-mode mobile flight results screen with a near-black background, soft violet primary and emerald confirmations — a modern, high-contrast travel booking UI. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/flight-results-mobile/raw)
- [Flight Search Results — Light](https://dotgui.org/examples/flight-search-results/) — mobile; A mobile flight search results screen on a warm off-white background with terracotta accents, listing fares in a calm, editorial travel-app style. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/flight-search-results/raw)
- [Headspace — Meditation](https://dotgui.org/examples/headspace-clone/) — mobile; A Headspace-inspired meditation home screen on a warm cream background with a friendly orange primary, offering calm, rounded cards for guided sessions. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/headspace-clone/raw)
- [iPad Video Editor](https://dotgui.org/examples/video-editor/) — mobile; A tablet video editor interface in dark mode, using near-black panels and a violet accent to frame the preview, timeline and clip tracks of a pro editing app. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/video-editor/raw)
- [Instagram — Feed](https://dotgui.org/examples/instagram-clone/) — mobile; An Instagram feed clone in dark mode — a pure-black background with layered grey surfaces — reproducing the stories bar, post cards and bottom tab navigation. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/instagram-clone/raw)
- [Lindholm Chair — Product Page](https://dotgui.org/examples/chair/) — mobile; A minimalist furniture product page for the Lindholm chair, set on a soft off-white background with muted taupe accents for a calm, Scandinavian retail feel. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/chair/raw)
- [Meridian — Flight Results](https://dotgui.org/examples/meridian-flight-results/) — mobile; Meridian, a clean flight results screen for mobile presenting airline itineraries, layovers and pricing in a minimal, legible booking layout. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/meridian-flight-results/raw)
- [Now Playing — Retro](https://dotgui.org/examples/player/) — mobile; A retro "now playing" mobile music player in oxblood red and cream over warm dust-brown surfaces, with a tactile, analog-inspired playback layout. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/player/raw)
- [Skeuomorphic Music Player](https://dotgui.org/examples/skeuomorphic-music/) — mobile; A skeuomorphic "now playing" music player for mobile — cream and near-black tones, textured dials and a record-inspired transport, evoking vintage hi-fi hardware. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/skeuomorphic-music/raw)
- [PostHog — Flight Search](https://dotgui.org/examples/posthog-flights/) — mobile; A flight search results screen in PostHog's house style: a putty-grey canvas, hedgehog-yellow primary and olive text for a friendly, product-analytics aesthetic. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/posthog-flights/raw)
- [PostHog — Mobile Analytics](https://dotgui.org/examples/posthog-analytics/) — mobile; A PostHog mobile analytics dashboard with charts and metrics on a putty-grey background accented in signature hedgehog yellow — data-dense but approachable. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/posthog-analytics/raw)
- [Pulse — Activity Rings](https://dotgui.org/examples/material-expressive-fitness/) — mobile; Pulse, a Material 3 Expressive fitness screen with bold move, exercise and stand rings in electric purple, pink and teal against a bright, playful layout. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/material-expressive-fitness/raw)
- [Snapchat — Camera](https://dotgui.org/examples/snapchat/) — mobile; A Snapchat camera screen with the signature bright-yellow brand color over a full-bleed camera view, glassy HUD controls and chat and stories badges. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/snapchat/raw)
- [Spotify — Playlist](https://dotgui.org/examples/spotify-playlist/) — mobile; A Spotify playlist screen in dark mode with a near-black background, signature Spotify green primary and a gradient header over the track list. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/spotify-playlist/raw)
- [Stride — Today](https://dotgui.org/examples/stride-today/) — mobile; A running app "today" dashboard in Material You, pairing a bright off-white background with a forest-green primary and lime accents for an energetic, outdoorsy look. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/stride-today/raw)
- [Whoop — Recovery Dashboard](https://dotgui.org/examples/whoop-dashboard/) — mobile; A WHOOP-style fitness dashboard in dark mode, using a near-black background and vivid recovery-green readouts to surface strain, sleep and recovery metrics. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/whoop-dashboard/raw)
- [.gui — Landing Page](https://dotgui.org/examples/dotgui-landing-page/) — web; A dark, high-contrast marketing landing page for the .gui format, built on a near-black canvas with subtle translucent borders and crisp typographic hierarchy. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/dotgui-landing-page/raw)
- [Drift](https://dotgui.org/examples/drift/) — web; Drift, a calm editorial web layout in warm greige tones with a muted teal accent, using generous whitespace and quiet typography for a slow, considered feel. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/drift/raw)
- [Echelon Atelier — Events](https://dotgui.org/examples/echelon-atelier-events/) — web; Echelon Atelier, an editorial event-production agency site in cream and espresso tones with refined serif typography for a luxury, boutique-studio feel. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/echelon-atelier-events/raw)
- [Figma — Editor](https://dotgui.org/examples/figma-clone/) — web; A Figma editor clone with the familiar dark-grey canvas, left layers panel, right properties inspector and blue selection accent of a design tool UI. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/figma-clone/raw)
- [Flight Results — Desktop](https://dotgui.org/examples/flight-results/) — web; A desktop flight results page in dark mode with a near-black background, violet primary and emerald confirmations, laying out fares and itineraries in wide rows. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/flight-results/raw)
- [Nexus — Event Booking](https://dotgui.org/examples/design-event-booking/) — web; Nexus, a dark, premium event booking page with a near-black background and warm gold primary, presenting sessions and ticketing in an upscale conference style. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/design-event-booking/raw)
- [Oscillate — Music Production](https://dotgui.org/examples/music-production-daw/) — web; Oscillate, a digital audio workstation in dark mode with layered near-black surfaces, mixer channels and an arrangement timeline for a professional DAW interface. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/music-production-daw/raw)
- [Premium Baby Accessories](https://dotgui.org/examples/premium-baby-accessories/) — web; An ecommerce storefront for premium baby accessories in warm beige and terracotta, with soft editorial product imagery and a gentle, boutique retail layout. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/premium-baby-accessories/raw)
- [Spotify — Desktop](https://dotgui.org/examples/spotify-desktop/) — web; A Spotify desktop app layout with the classic black sidebar, card grid and now-playing bar, accented in Spotify green — a full media-player web interface. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/spotify-desktop/raw)
- [Sundial Studio](https://dotgui.org/examples/sundial-studio/) — web; Sundial Studio, a creative agency landing page on a warm cream background with a bold red-orange accent, combining editorial type with a sunlit, tactile mood. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/sundial-studio/raw)
- [The Far Field](https://dotgui.org/examples/farfield/) — web; The Far Field, a moody editorial site on deep forest-grey surfaces with a soft sage accent, pairing muted nature tones with restrained, literary typography. · [raw source](https://dotgui.org/examples/farfield/raw)
